supporting_quotes: Extracting Business Process Entities and Relations from Text Using Pre-trained Language Models and In-Context Learning
Abstract. The extraction of business processes elements from textual documents is a research area which still lacks the ability to scale to the variety of real-world texts.

In this paper we explore, for the first time in literature, the feasibility of using in-context learning over the pre-trained language models to perform process extraction from textual documents in a conversational fashion.
criterion_assessments.notes: Title and abstract are in English and describe a full-text article with empirical study; full text is available in English.

supporting_quotes: In-context Learning to Process Extraction from Text
The experiments we have conducted provide two types of insights.
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper reports empirical assessment of a GPT-3 based approach for process extraction, indicating primary research with experiments.

supporting_quotes: In this paper we explore, for the first time in literature, the feasibility of using in-context learning over the pre-trained language models to perform process extraction from textual documents in a conversational fashion.
we focus on these four elements as they constitute the basic building blocks on any business process model, they enable the construction of a basic structured representation.

the extraction of activities, participants, the performing relation between a participant and the activity(ies) it performs, and the sequence relation between activities (hereafter directly follow relation).
criterion_assessments.notes: The work explicitly targets NLP-based process extraction from text and defines the elements to be extracted (activities, participants, performing relation, and directly follows), satisfying the core scope.

supporting_quotes: The starting point is a set of process elements (entities and/or relationships) we aim at extracting, and the first building block of the approach is the formulation of a series of incremental questions posed to the GPT-3 model in a sequential manner which enable the extraction of those specific entities and relationships.
We evaluated the proposed approach by extracting activities, participants, the performing relation, and the directly follow relation as illustrated in Sect. 3.1.

(T1) extract activities, using question Q1 as task instruction in the prompt-template; (T2) extract participants and the performs relation, using a customized question Q2 for each input activity as task instruction in the prompt-template; (T3) extract the directly follow relation using a customized question Q3 for each pair of input activities as task instruction in the prompt-template.
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper presents a concrete method (prompt-based in-context learning pipeline) and reports an empirical assessment with defined tasks and evaluation.
No evidence of failure to meet full-paper/English/full-text criteria; full text is English and present.

Paper specifically covers NLP-enabled process extraction from natural-language text; within target scope.
The work includes concrete methods and empirical validation; not superficial.

supporting_quotes: The modelling process considers the following steps: 1) Elicitation of process components from texts. 2) Elicitation Check: A semi-automated mapping of process components to natural descriptions may potentially retrieve false positives and false negatives.
The semi-automatic method makes use of the NLP module to perform extraction, visualisation and learning of roles, activities and constraints.
c) Quality Control & Documentation Maintenance

The workbench has a number of tools to check for correctness of the generated processes. First, the dead-end analyzer implements the checks for deadlock and livelock-freedom for DCR graphs in [15]. The second refers to semantic correctness. Test-driven development [16], [20] allows engineers to define scenarios describing valid and invalid process traces. Scenarios will be tested against the current model, suggesting whether some constraints are necessary (resp. missing).

Due to the short release time, we have not yet validated the advantages of automatic suggestions with bigger datasets, but in our current experiments we have been able to identify roles, activities and constraints that closely resemble those established by humans3.

supporting_quotes: Abstract: Process Modeling has been a very active research topic for the last decades. One of its main issues is the externalization of knowledge and its acquisition for further use, as this remains deeply related to the quality of the resulting process models produced by this task.

supporting_quotes: In this section, we present three baselines we developed to provide preliminary results obtained on the dataset and also to show how the dataset can be used to test different extraction approaches.

Baseline 1 (B1): by starting from the raw text (i.e., no information related to process elements or relations has been used), a CRF-based approach has been used for building a model to support the extraction of single entities
Baseline 2 (B2): by starting from the existing gold information concerning the annotation of process elements, a RB strategy has been used for detecting relations between entities.
Baseline 3 (B3): this baseline relies on the output of B1 concerning the annotations of process elements. Then, a RB strategy has been used for detecting relations between entities.

supporting_quotes: Extracting Decision Model Components from Natural Language Text for Automated Business Decision Modelling
This paper is structured as follows ... The last section summarizes the paper with the conclusion.
The full text contains typical research paper sections: Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Proposed Solution, Results, Conclusion
The full text is in English and contains full methodological and experimental details.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text is a full English research article with complete text and appropriate scientific structure.

supporting_quotes: This research investigates state-of-the-art NLP techniques, Rule-based approaches, and ML-based approaches in relevant domains.
We provide a general framework, Text2DMN, to automatically convert decision descriptions to decision models.
We experiment with a prototype tool to test the proposed solution to extract decision model component from text.
Preliminary results ... with precision, recall, and F1 metrics for dependency extractor and logic extractor.
Contributions include novel NLP application and prototype implementation, indicating original research.
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper reports original methodology development and empirical evaluation, not a survey or secondary work.

supporting_quotes: The main idea is that from the syntactic and grammatical structure of a sentence, the components of a decision model can be derived (i.e., rules, concepts, dependencies, and constraints) to assemble this information as the decision model in the DMN standard.
We provide a general framework, Text2DMN, to automatically convert the decision descriptions to the Decision Models.
The focus is on extracting decision model components from natural language texts (rules, logic, dependencies) to generate DMN decision models.
The paper deals with natural language processing to extract process elements related to decision modeling from textual artifacts (documents, policies).
criterion_assessments.notes: The work clearly focuses on NLP to extract process-related decision models from natural language text.

supporting_quotes: We provide a general framework, Text2DMN, which includes three phases: text selection, processing, and model generation.
We implemented a prototype tool integrating rule-based NLP with Spacy and neuralcoref.
Preliminary results include precision, recall, and F1-score metrics for dependency tuple extraction (F1 = 0.867) and logic extraction (F1 = 0.671).
Experiments were conducted on a test dataset of 20 example texts with manual annotation.
Evaluation metrics and plans for further tool development and hybrid ML approaches are described.
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper presents a concrete method with detailed implementation and empirical evaluation using precision/recall metrics.

supporting_quotes: Process extraction from text is an important task of process discovery, for which various approaches have been developed in recent years.
We present our new resource, including a variety of baselines to benchmark the difficulty and challenges of business process extraction from text.
The dataset, annotation guidelines, and inception schema are freely available.
The text is fully in English and includes detailed methodology, dataset annotation, and baseline experiments.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text is a full English research article with full text available.

supporting_quotes: The contributions of this work are: 1. We provide a new reference corpus, annotation schema, and guidelines for the task of annotating business process models in running text.
We quantify the difficulty of fundamental information extraction tasks for process model extraction by deploying a variety of baselines on our annotated data.
We developed three baselines to provide preliminary results obtained on the dataset and to show how the dataset can be used to test different extraction approaches.
criterion_assessments.notes: Paper presents original dataset creation and baseline experiments, confirming primary original research.

supporting_quotes: Process extraction from text is an important task of process discovery.

criterion_assessments.notes: Full-text English Doctoral Consortium article is available and clearly presented.

supporting_quotes: The aim of the present research is to explore how NLP can be applied in the BPM domain in order to automatically generate business process models from existing documentation within an organization.
The contributions will be considered: ... Novel Transformation Approach.
The prototype tool as a software project will be written in Java and will combine three major independent linguistic tools...
criterion_assessments.notes: Paper describes an original research agenda, prototype development and planned contributions (novel transformation approach, tool, dataset, evaluation framework).

supporting_quotes: The main idea is that from the syntactic and grammatical structure of a sentence, the components of a business process model can be derived (i.e. activities, resources, tasks, patterns).
The extraction can be achieved by applying well known NLP techniques such as Part of Speech tagging, Named Entity Recognition and Co-reference Resolution.
The result would be a business process model depicted using BPMN – a dedicated business process modeling technique.
criterion_assessments.notes: Full text explicitly targets NLP-driven extraction/transformation of natural-language text into BPMN process models and related components.

supporting_quotes: The solution is implemented as a Java project and combines different computational linguistics tools.

supporting_quotes: Abstract. One of the main promises of process conformance is the opportunity to align normative processes (i.e. how the process should behave) and event logs (i.e. how does the process actually behaves).
Key words: Natural Language Processing, Normative Processes, Process Discovery, Process Conformance
criterion_assessments.notes: Full text is available in English and structured as a standard research article (abstract, sections, references).

supporting_quotes: The challenges reported in this paper result from 4 years of interactions between the author and municipal sectors in Denmark and Italy in the formalization of laws using DCR graphs in the EcoKnow project [10].
Our initial experiments in the Danish laws included annotations of 55 articles from the danish administrative acts for family and social services [13].
criterion_assessments.notes: Paper reports original work: data collection/annotation and practitioner interactions over a multi-year project, consistent with primary research rather than purely a survey.

supporting_quotes: Recent developments advocate the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) to process model discovery from texts.
NLP is a key enabling technology for solving our question. Instead of discovery from event logs, NLP allows the identification of processes from texts.
criterion_assessments.notes: The full text explicitly addresses NLP-based textual process discovery and mapping texts (laws) to normative/process models.

supporting_quotes: They resulted in the elicitation of an annotation guideline as an initial step to create corpora containing manually assigned process-law pairs [12].
Our initial experiments in the Danish laws included annotations of 55 articles from the danish administrative acts for family and social services [13].
Both groups performed textual annotations of laws into process elements, with a follow-up including interviews and think-out-loud sessions.
counter_quotes: Interviews and think-out-loud sessions followed the annotations, providing validation and challenge identification.

supporting_quotes: Abstract— In this paper, we report recent advances on user support for declarative process generation from natural language descriptions.
2019 IEEE 23rd International Enterprise Distributed Object Computing Workshop (EDOCW)
The text is a full research article with sections including Introduction, System Overview, Related Work, and Concluding Remarks.
criterion_assessments.notes: Full English-language research article with complete full text and standard paper structure.

supporting_quotes: In this paper, we report recent advances on user support for declarative process generation from natural language descriptions.
In this paper we present efforts in providing assistance for users to automate process highlights.

The Process Highlighter is a hybrid-modelling tool ... The principal change is the inclusion of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support users in the identification of roles, activities and constraints.
criterion_assessments.notes: Paper presents original system development, methodological contributions, and empirical observations; it is primary research rather than a review.

supporting_quotes: The principal change is the inclusion of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support users in the identification of roles, activities and constraints.
The semi-automatic method makes use of the NLP module to perform extraction, visualisation and learning of roles, activities and constraints.
The process highlighter presents suggestions for process model components based in this data.
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper explicitly describes NLP-enabled extraction/alignment of roles, activities and relations from natural-language process descriptions to create declarative process models.

supporting_quotes: The NLP module relies on a mixed dataset. On the one hand, it uses the Wordnet pre-trained dataset [14] ... In addition, the NLP module interacts with a dataset containing roles, activities, and relations (R-A-R in Fig. 1). This dataset is trained via user interactions: each suggestion accepted/rejected via the process highlighter changes the accuracy of the suggestions presented.

The semi-automatic method makes use of the NLP module to perform extraction, visualisation and learning of roles, activities and constraints. Instead of performing model extraction, our method provides alignment suggestions.

After a year since its initial release, we have collected experiences from the use of the highlighter in these different realms. They come in the form of empirical evaluations of the tool [3], and discussions with users.

The workbench has a number of tools to check for correctness of the generated processes. First, the dead-end analyzer implements the checks for deadlock and livelock-freedom for DCR graphs in [15]. ... Test-driven development [16], [20] allows engineers to define scenarios describing valid and invalid process traces. Scenarios will be tested against the current model...
counter_quotes: Due to the short release time, we have not yet validated the advantages of automatic suggestions with bigger datasets, but in our current experiments we have been able to identify roles, activities and constraints that closely resemble those established by humans3.
criterion_assessments.notes: The paper describes a concrete system architecture, datasets (WordNet and a user-trained R-A-R), algorithmic/interaction steps (elicitation, elicitation check, quality control), and reports empirical evaluations/observations with users and initial experiments. Although large-scale benchmark validation is noted as pending, the presence of implemented methods plus empirical evaluations satisfies the criterion for concrete method and empirical validation at Stage 2.
